I would stay with the local two-crop system: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. In Quzhou, that is the safest way for me to keep grain output steady, use my land all year, and fit the weather. Wheat needs more irrigation because winter and spring are dry here, while maize can lean more on summer rain. I would not switch into a riskier cash crop this year because I am 57, I know this wheat-maize cycle well, and I would rather run a familiar system with stable yield than chase something uncertain. I would use improved seed, keep fertilizer moderate instead of pushing it too hard, return straw where I can, plough before wheat to loosen the soil, and use no-tillage for maize after wheat so I can sow fast and hold moisture. I would spray only when needed, mainly to protect the wheat in spring and keep maize clean in the early stage. Since no land size was given, I am expressing my decision as a 10 mu farm plan.

I’m grounding this in local Quzhou/Hebei sources on the dominant wheat-maize rotation and recent county yield and input levels: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5290742/ , https://qzsyz.cau.edu.cn/art/2024/2/25/art_46232_1012984.html , https://qzsyz.cau.edu.cn/art/2024/10/8/art_46317_1039835.html
